memory: Internal back surface plus thin cavity resonance cause the secondary flip. Absorber must be conformal and impedance-matched. Empirically: 3 mm open-cell melamine is the practical minimum. New finding: conformal bonding pressure ≈20 kPa collapses the discontinuity while keeping direct arrival loss ≤3%; pressures ≲5 kPa give only partial suppression; pressures ≳60–80 kPa increase direct loss. Standing correction: thickness alone insufficient; contact pressure is a separate control variable. Current aim: relate these pressure thresholds to the absorber's surface acoustic impedance at 500 kHz.
openQuestion: What is the absorber's normal acoustic impedance at 500 kHz corresponding to ≥85% suppression, and how to measure Za precisely?
